findings.source_quote: Εἰ καὶ τῇ γενέσει οὐ ταὐτόν ἐστιν;
findings.english_quote: Even if it is the same in respect of generation?
findings.issue: The affirmative conditional does not faithfully represent οὐ. Taking εἰ καί concessively gives ‘even if it is not the same’; taking the construction as a negative question would require an explicit negative question in English. The note's proposed literal wording combines these constructions awkwardly and does not disclose the straightforward concessive reading with nonidentity.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose: ‘Even if it is not the same in respect of generation?’ Explain that εἰ καί is taken concessively in response to the preceding distinction. If a negative question seeking assent is retained as an alternative, give that alternative explicitly, rather than converting it into an affirmative conditional. The replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: τὸ λεγόμενον ὄνομα τοῦ μὴ λεγομένου πρόοδός ἐστιν
findings.english_quote: the spoken name is an advance toward the unspoken one
findings.issue: The directional rendering is defensible as a contextual account of movement from the public designation to the unspoken name, but the note does not disclose the material alternative suggested by πρόοδος with the genitive: the spoken name is a going-forth or outward expression of the unspoken name. Merely identifying a movement metaphor does not explain this difference in direction.
findings.suggested_revision: Expand the source-quoted note to preserve ‘the spoken name is a going-forth of the unspoken one’ as an alternative. Explain that ‘advance toward’ was chosen because the preceding conditional traces the attachment of the spoken name to the consequent attachment of the unspoken name. Alternatively, propose a source-transparent main rendering with ‘advance of’ or ‘going-forth of’ and document its interpretation. Any revised wording or disclosure requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ὡς ἐπὶ μοιχείας πνευματικῆς τῆς κατὰ σάρκα χείρονος ὑπαρχούσης
findings.english_quote: as in the case of spiritual adultery, which is worse than adultery according to the flesh
findings.issue: The main rendering defensibly takes τῆς κατὰ σάρκα as the genitive of comparison and attaches χείρονος ὑπαρχούσης to spiritual adultery. However, the sequence also permits taking τῆς κατὰ σάρκα as the subject of a genitive absolute: ‘adultery according to the flesh being worse.’ That materially different comparison is not disclosed in the notes.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the proposed main reading only with a source-quoted note explaining its comparative-genitive construction and preserving the alternative ‘adultery according to the flesh being worse.’ State that the main reading is favored because the surrounding rebuke presents Simon's impiety as especially serious. This is an attachment ambiguity, not an unverified printing defect; the revised disclosure requires fresh review.
